title: Long baseline (WISE 2010 vs SPHEREx 2025 to 2026)
band_note: WISE W1 (3.4 µm) and W2 (4.6 µm) are broad filters; the SPHEREx side stacks its 2.9 to 3.8 µm and 4.0 to 5.0 µm channels, so brightness and colour differ a little but positions do not.
normalisation: Each image is stretched between its own 10th and 99.5th percentile (asinh), because WISE counts and SPHEREx MJy/sr are different units.

labels.text: Saturated core masked in the SPHEREx frame
The diagonal streak in the 2010 frames is a WISE artefact from bright ε Indi A, just west of the field, not a moving source
Blended with a Gaia field star at short wavelengths: at 2.9 to 3.8 µm the SPHEREx light at the 2025 position is partly that star
Barely detected by WISE in W1 in 2010 (peak S/N about 7). Use W2, where it is clear in both epochs
A G=16.3 Gaia star sits 8″ from the 2025 position and adds some light at 4 to 5 µm
No visible motion expected: 0.5″ in 16 years (0.07 px). RW Aur is a variable young star, so brightness differences are real
